# R427 — Layer-major bulk-upload candidate lifetime and safety audit

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source audit of the completed candidate in the new bulk-upload worktree. No build, test, lint, AST, GPU, profiler, process/service action, cleanup, or source edit. Main's active official quiet benchmark was not inspected or touched.

## Decision

Static review finds the core bulk path internally consistent for its explicit narrow eligibility: 512-expert native layout, owned single-Runtime Host-USM source span, private one-layer cache, no segmented/VMM backing, active-stride table scoped to that cache, blocking checked full-layer copy, then host residency publication. Existing outer layer-reuse `m.cs` drain is sufficient for the prior layer's actual cache readers in this route: `layer_ready` requires all experts resident and the private path sets `m.ring=0`; nonresident staging on `m.copy` is therefore skipped, while native dequant, fallback compute, MMQ resident-to-ring copies, group gathers and their consumer events all submit on `m.cs`. `m.copy` is still drained at admission and restore, and `run_impl` joins/drains its source/stager work before returning. No extra wait is indicated by source.

I found no definite source-level correctness defect in the successful-copy/fallback/retirement flow. The maximum 1,363,148,800-byte single-copy behavior and the complete layer-major path remain unbuilt and unmeasured; this audit establishes neither runtime acceptance, numerical correctness, speed, nor that a successful full-size copy will be available on the target driver. The opt-in switch is exact `STRATA_PREFILL_LAYER_BULK_COPY=1`; default selection stays on the existing per-expert copy path. There is a small default-off instrumentation change: new logical-byte and copy-call counters still increment in the legacy fallback loop, and `PrefillStats` grows by four counters. Those counters are not printed when the option is off, but the per-copy counter increments sit inside the existing `ms_experts_host` interval; treat zero-cost default-off behavior as unproven.

## Source ownership and view validity

`ExpertSource::layer_span()` defaults to decline (`include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp:134-135`). The span carries a data pointer, exact bytes, per-expert stride, layer/expert count and source-owner pointer; its contract lasts until source close/destruction, including across `blob()` calls (`:127-135`). Only `ArenaExpertSource` overrides it. Its layer predicate requires the recorded owned-span mode, live arena, no mmap view, native geometry, exactly 512 experts, valid layer indices in both metadata arrays, and a bounded layer against the source's total blob count (`src/core/expert_source.cpp:2704-2718`). It checks `stride != 0`, 256-byte alignment and `stride*512` overflow, then bounds `[layer_offset, layer_offset+bytes)` against layout total. Finally, `PinnedArena::owned_host_range()` requires the full requested range to fit in one owned allocation piece, `Runtime::owner(pointer) == &Runtime::get()`, and `usm::alloc::host` in that Runtime context (`src/core/pinned.cpp:346-362`). The Host-USM constructor allocates one block per layer from that exact Runtime context (`:132-158`), with the source's layer payload plus padding, so this establishes one continuous copy source for the layer.

The eligibility bit is set only after the Host-USM source path finishes setup, and only for `host_usm && shared_arena_file.empty()` (`src/core/expert_source.cpp:2608`). `STRATA_ARENA_MMAP` exits through a mapped-file path without setting it; the split-registration `register_on()` explicitly clears it (`:2388`); shared arena use excludes it. A normal registered mapping is not accepted merely because it is pinned. `owned_host_range()` additionally rejects another context or non-Host-USM allocation. Thus mmap, shared-file, transient, host-registration-only, and multi-device re-registration decline to the old per-expert path.

`consumed_layer_span()` checks source identity, 512 experts and signed counter headroom before adding 512 reads (`expert_source.cpp:2720-2725`). The caller invokes it only after `gpu::copy` has returned success; the normal `blob()` path increments reads one expert at a time (`:2737+`). A noneligible span does not consume reads and its 512 per-expert fallback calls retain the old accounting. The current caller passes the exact span returned from this source through `valid_span` and verifies `span.layer` first; there is no second call site that could count an unconsumed span.

## Private active cache and all relevant consumers

`open_private_layer_sized()` accepts only one layer, 512 uniform positive 256-byte-aligned slots, with multiplication bounds, and then uses the ordinary allocator (`src/core/expert_cache.cpp:517-526`). `set_private_layer_stride()` is limited to that private non-phase cache, requires a live ordinary allocation with no VMM/segments, all 512 slots live and the 513-entry reserved offset array, then asks `layer_bulk::compact()` to validate drained-reader assertion, sorted reserved extents, stride capacity and total compact extent before setting active stride (`:528-534`; `include/strata/core/layer_bulk_layout.hpp:11-29`). `restore_private_layer_layout()` disables only the active view (`expert_cache.cpp:536-539`). The 512-entry active offsets are a separate fixed `std::array`; reserved `off_` stays unchanged. `device_slot()` uses active offsets only when the active stride is set (`:609-623`); `slot_offsets()`/`slot_offset()` return active view offsets for this private view, while `bytes()`, `full_bytes()`, `bytes_of()` and backing extent continue to use reserved offsets. Private caches reject shrink/grow; active fill/verify APIs reject lengths larger than the active slot view (`:352-398, 628-710`). No cache reallocates while changing layer stride.

`run_layer_major()` selects this cache only when the opt-in is on, there are 512 experts and `MAXBLOB` is 256-byte aligned; otherwise it opens the previous `open_sized(MAXBLOB*512)` cache (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1504-1513`). Every next layer begins with the existing checked `stream_sync(m.cs)`, clears stale residency before touching layout, asks the source for a span, validates owner/layer/count/exact byte extent, then prepares the private active stride (`:1519-1533`). `layer_ready()` checks all 512 `residency[e] == e` and every active offset delta is at least the actual layer blob width before each chunk (`prefill.cpp:1686-1691`, `include/strata/prefill/layer_major.hpp:86-91`).

The only private-cache compute consumers use the public `device_slot(residency)` pointer:

- Native batch builds local `nd_blob[]` from `blob_dev` and adds `NativeFmt`'s actual `up_off/down_off`; byte bounds use `f.bytes`, row payloads, and `layout.blob_bytes(layer)` (`prefill.cpp:2630-2658, 2849-2870`). It does not reconstruct expert addresses from `e*MAXBLOB`.
- Native non-batch and fallback compute take `device_slot()` for resident routes (`:2895, 2942, 3167, 3212`) and pass it to actual-format dequant/product code. The per-layer view therefore needs to change pointer starts, not format payload sizes.
- MMQ's `MMQ_SLOT()` remains a different max-sized/aligned scratch-ring stride (`:637-643`). A resident expert is copied into that ring using the actual `blob_bytes(layer)` on `m.cs` (`:2841-2848`, mirrored route around `3127-3134`); `Product::expert_bytes` then uses `MMQ_SLOT()` and its down offset (`:2867-2884`). Gather receives explicit resident `blob_dev` pointers and actual `NativeFmt` extents (`:2768-2777`). Compact cache layout does not require changing MMQ ring layout.
- Shared BF16 expert weights are ordinary model weights, not cache slots (`:2252-2264`). CPU-share candidate selection excludes every resident expert (`:2333-2346`); the private layer cache publishes all 512 residents before `run_impl`, so the current layer has no CPU source miss to hand off. Streamed nonresident stage/ring pointers remain their existing max-sized scratch layout and are not this active cache.

The decode/drive/verify offset aliases point at the ordinary `xcache`, not the temporary `layer_cache`: `generate.cpp:4940-4944` binds Drive's base/blob/offset table, split stages retain those table pointers (`:6160-6181`), and the verifier gets an `xcache.slot_offsets()` table (`:6080-6088, 11330-11339`). `expert_source.cpp:1834-1835` consumes the Drive table; `Verifier::init` copies verify offsets into its own device table (`src/core/verify.cpp:456-459`). `run_layer_major` swaps only `Prefill::Impl::m.cache/m.host_res` to the private objects (`prefill.cpp:1515-1517`) and its `Restore` restores them after both compute and copy stream drains (`:1480-1497`). The active table is therefore not captured by Drive, split drive, phase cache, verifier, token graph or device offset tables. No stale alias to the private table was found.

## Copy, fallback, publication and lifetime ordering

`core::layer_bulk::valid_span()` requires non-null data/owner, expected owner identity, exactly 512 experts, aligned stride equal to the current real layer width, overflow-safe geometry and exact `bytes == stride*512` (`layer_bulk_layout.hpp:20-25`). If source or layout eligibility declines, `restore_private_layer_layout(true)` switches `device_slot` back to the reserved MAXBLOB offsets before the first fallback write (`prefill.cpp:1529-1551`). The caller's `readers_drained=true` comes from the existing pre-layer `m.cs` synchronization; previous resident MMQ ring copies and native/fallback readers are all queued on `m.cs`. The in-layer route has `m.ring==0` enforced by `layer_ready`, while streamed staging on `m.copy` is entered only for nonresident experts and `stream_all` requires `m.ring > STAGE` (`prefill.cpp:1686-1691, 1797+`). Since all 512 are resident, it skips those `m.copy` readers. `run_impl`'s per-layer body ends with an existing checked `m.cs` sync (`:3451+`) and joins its host issuer/stager work before return (`:3310-3320`); there is no outstanding source-side reader at the outer layer boundary. `m.copy` is also drained before admission and during the restore guard (`:1444-1446, 1482-1487`), so no extra drain was proposed.

On the bulk branch, the sole new operation is blocking `gpu::copy(layer_cache.device_slot(0), span.data, span.bytes)`; `gpu::copy` submits one `memcpy` to the Runtime compute queue and waits its returned event before returning (`src/core/gpu.cpp:244-255`). The host span remains owned until `ArenaExpertSource::close`; the prefill source lives through the request and the copy is synchronous. `complete_copy` runs its publish callback only if the copy callable returned true (`layer_bulk_layout.hpp:27-30`). The callback then accounts 512 source reads and logical stats. After the branch completes successfully, the loop fills the host residency table for all experts (`prefill.cpp:1536-1578`). A copy failure does not invoke fallback or publish residency: `publication::cleanup_require` is fail-stop for uncertain completion, so stack owners are not unwound as if the cache were safe. An eligibility decline happens before copy and takes the regular per-expert copy path at max-stride destinations. This satisfies no retry after a possibly partial/uncertain bulk write.

After the final layer `Restore` invokes the checked compute and copy drains and finishes staging before restoring old cache/residency/callback pointers. If either completion is unknown, its cleanup failure path terminates before returning/freeing the private cache, residual buffers or stack residency (`prefill.cpp:1480-1497`; `layer_major.hpp:95-100`). `ExpertCache::close()` itself is not a queue-retirement proof, so retaining this outer guard is essential.

## Default-off behavior and unverified facts

`bulk_copy_requested()` accepts only the exact string `"1"` and is frozen by its function-local static (`include/strata/prefill/layer_major.hpp:16-22`). When false, `private_layout` is false and the same reserved `open_sized` path and 512 checked per-expert copies run. The upload summary is guarded by `if (bulk_copy)` (`prefill.cpp:1604-1608`), and no other output consumer of the new counters exists in source. However, fallback increments the new `layer_upload_copy_calls` counter unconditionally (`:1563-1568`) and accumulates new logical-byte counters after every layer (`:1571-1576`); four fields also enlarge `PrefillStats`. This is a small source-observable default-off overhead and should be measured or gated if strict no-regression is required. No source change was made.

The supplied pre-candidate 32K GEN evidence (24,576 per-expert calls, 50,292,326,400 logical bytes, 14,961.143 ms combined source+checked-copy host wall) motivates testing only; it is not the bulk path's byte/call result or pure PCIe time. One actual layer reaches `512*MAXBLOB = 1,363,148,800` bytes. This candidate has not been built or tested, and the full-size single Host-USM copy, return-time semantics on the target driver, output equality under compact stride, source-counter result, allocator memory admission, and quiet performance remain unproven. Parent reports Main's official quiet benchmark is active under handle 72851; no live output or process state was read here.
